Comparative Genomics · Internal Report

Two Lipid-Producing Strains, One Ancestor, and a Duplicated Mevalonate Kinase

A whole-genome comparison of mutant strain HS6 against the newly PacBio-sequenced isolate Schizochytrium sp. #7 — testing whether HS6's lipid-pathway divergence from wild type is mirrored, or absent, in an independent strain.

⚠ Correction — 2026-07-30, post-publication

A parameter bug in the original genome-level verification step (Section 2/3) caused most real gene matches to be missed, and has been fixed. The verification used diamond blastx with --max-target-seqs 1 against a whole genome split into 30–34 scaffold queries — which reports only the single best-scoring protein per scaffold, capping total possible hits at the scaffold count regardless of how many genes actually matched. Rerunning with a corrected, generous --max-target-seqs changed the confirmed-unique counts substantially:

FindingOriginally reportedCorrected
Genuinely #7-unique genes (of 487 candidates)472 (96.9%)102 (21.0%)
Genuinely HS6-unique genes (of 4,012 candidates)3,983 (99.3%)47 (1.2%)
Of the 41 SwissProt-credible HS6-unique genes, still absent from #741 (100%)1 (2.4%)

Two downstream conclusions do not survive this correction and are struck through in place below: the 5.6× transposon/recombination enrichment in Section 3, and all three "lipid-adjacent" candidate genes in the original Section 6 — all three (g8002, g6581, g5706) turned out to be present in strain #7's genome too, just uncalled by its gene-prediction pipeline, the same failure mode as the dgat2_1 case already documented in Section 2. Sections 1, 4, 5, and 7 use independent methods (minimap2 alignment, protein-vs-protein RBH, direct PacBio read realignment) unaffected by this bug and are unchanged.

00

Executive summary

Strain #7 is not a distant relative — it is a near-identical sibling of HS6, sharing 98.9% genome-wide sequence identity and near-complete synteny. That closeness is what makes the differences worth trusting: when two genomes this similar diverge at a specific locus, the divergence is more likely to be real biology than noise.

Relatedness
Same species, high-confidence synteny across 97–98% of both assemblies, in blocks up to 1.29 Mb.
Core lipid pathway
Every one of the 15 previously-characterized DHA/PUFA and carotenoid-precursor genes is single-copy and >96.5% identical in both strains — this machinery is not where the strains diverge.
Real divergence
After correcting a verification bug (see notice above), only ~2% of "unique" gene calls survive as genuinely strain-specific — almost everything is annotation-pipeline noise, and no reliable functional-category signal remains in what's left.
The one metabolic lead
A region carrying mevalonate kinase shows 2× PacBio read depth in HS6 only — normal single-copy depth in #7's homologous contig — and MVK trends downward in HS6's own RNA-seq.

The sections below walk through the evidence in the order it was built: first establishing how closely related the strains are (so the rest of the comparison has a reliable baseline), then separating genuine gene-content differences from annotation-pipeline noise, then testing the specific pathway everyone cares about, and finally following the one lead that survived every check.

Most #7 contigs map cleanly onto a single HS6 scaffold end-to-end. Where a contig splits across two scaffolds (e.g. #7's contig1 → HS6 Scaffolds_23 + Scaffolds_14), the split sits at a scaffold boundary on the HS6 side — consistent with a scaffolding-join difference between the two independent assemblies rather than a true structural rearrangement.

Is this chromosome-level? And where's the mitochondrion?

HS6's 34 scaffolds were screened for the canonical eukaryotic telomeric repeat (TTAGGG/CCCTAA) at both ends:

Complete chromosomes
14 of 34 scaffolds are telomere-capped at both ends — genuine telomere-to-telomere assemblies, not just large contigs.
Partial
14 have a confirmed telomere at one end only; the other end is an assembly break or unresolved repeat.
Unresolved
6 scaffolds (0, 3, 12, 27, 31, 32) show no telomere at either end — more likely genuine fragments.

No independent karyotype/cytology data exists for this organism, so this confirms 14 complete chromosomes, not a total chromosome count.

Separately: HS6's mitochondrial genome is not among the 34 scaffolds. The vendor's raw taxonomy-screening output (pre-dating the final "decontaminated" assembly) contains a contig explicitly labeled mt — 31,487 bp, GC 33.9% (vs. 44–46% for every nuclear contig), classified as Schizochytrium sp. TIO1101. It was filtered out during decontamination before delivery, consistent with the decont-labeled assembly filenames throughout the working files. By contrast, strain #7's delivery still carries its likely mitochondrial contig (the low-GC, 240×-depth contig29 flagged in Section 5) — the two vendor runs were decontaminated to different standards.

02

Gene content & annotation truth

The raw numbers looked dramatic. Most of that drama turned out to be two different annotation pipelines disagreeing with each other, not two genomes disagreeing with biology.

HS6 (BRAKER/AUGUSTUS, ab initio) and strain #7 (MAKER/Seqping, evidence-combined) were annotated by fundamentally different pipelines with different philosophies — one predicts genes from sequence signal alone, the other combines multiple predictors and BLAST evidence. A naive reciprocal-best-hit (RBH) comparison between their protein sets found:

CountInterpretation before verification
1:1 reciprocal-best-hit orthologs11,463Core shared gene set
HS6 genes, no hit in #74,012"HS6-specific gene content"?
#7 genes, no hit in HS6487"#7-specific gene content"?

A 4,012-gene "HS6-specific" set would be an extraordinary finding for two strains that are 98.9% identical genome-wide. It didn't survive scrutiny.

Stress-testing the HS6-unique list

Step 1 — external homology check
Of the 4,012 "HS6-unique" proteins, only 41 (1.0%) have any hit against SwissProt at all. Real genes — even lineage-specific ones — usually show some distant homology in a comprehensive database. A 99% miss rate points to spurious gene calls, not novel biology.
Step 2 — genome-level re-check (not just protein-vs-protein)
All 4,012 sequences were searched directly against #7's raw genome via 6-frame translation (diamond blastx), bypassing #7's gene models entirely. 3,965 of 4,012 matched somewhere in the genome — leaving only 47 genuinely unmatched (an earlier, buggy run of this same check under-counted matches severely; see the correction notice above). This check surfaced a case worth naming directly (below).
Step 3 — the dgat2_1 false alarm
A strain #7 gene annotated dgat2_1 (a diacylglycerol acyltransferase — the terminal enzyme of triacylglycerol synthesis) initially looked #7-specific, with zero protein-level hit anywhere in HS6. Direct 6-frame search against HS6's raw genome found the identical 517-aa sequence at 100% identity, full length, at Scaffolds_21:1,046,076–1,047,626. The gene is present in HS6 — BRAKER simply never called it. This is exactly the failure mode Step 2 exists to catch.
Step 4 — the surviving, doubly-confirmed set
Intersecting the SwissProt-credible 41 with the genome-verified absent set: only 1 of 41 overlaps (g6782, a distant match to a viral major capsid protein — 22.7% identity, not metabolically relevant). The other 40, including all three genes originally flagged as "lipid-adjacent," are present in #7's raw genome sequence and simply weren't called as genes by its MAKER pipeline. The defensible HS6-unique list is 1 gene, not 41.

The mirror check: #7-unique genes

Run the same two-step verification on the 487 "#7-unique" genes: 102 of 487 (21.0%) are confirmed genuinely absent from HS6's genome at the sequence level — the rest, including dgat2_1, are annotation gaps like the one documented in Step 3, just discovered on the other side of the comparison. Strain #7's pipeline is still the more conservative of the two (it over-predicts far less than BRAKER does), but "unannotated in the other strain" turned out to be a bigger contributor to both "unique" lists than real absence, in both directions.

Reading this table

Two very different-looking numbers (4,012 vs. 487) collapse to nearly the same small residual once verified against raw genome sequence (47 vs. 102) — both pipelines over-call genes relative to what's actually strain-specific, BRAKER far more severely than MAKER. The takeaway isn't just "BRAKER over-calls genes" (though it clearly does — see the 1%-SwissProt-hit-rate finding above, which is unaffected by the verification bug). It's that gene-content "uniqueness" claims between differently-annotated genomes need a genome-level check, done correctly, before they mean anything — a lesson this report had to learn twice, the second time on itself (see the correction notice above).

Independent cross-check: formal orthogroup inference

Everything above used reciprocal-best-hit (RBH), a fast but simplified stand-in for real orthology inference. A full OrthoFinder run (proper orthogroup clustering, not just best-hit pairs) gives an independent read on the same question:

Single-copy orthogroups
10,542 — close to the 11,463 RBH pairs from the same two proteomes, cross-validating the core shared gene set with a different method.
Species-specific orthogroups
HS6: 68 orthogroups / 349 genes. #7: 53 orthogroups / 467 genes — same order of magnitude as this report's corrected 47/102, not the original buggy 3,983/472.
Unassigned genes
HS6: 23.8% of genes cluster into no orthogroup at all vs. 2.7% for #7 — a third, independent line of evidence for the BRAKER over-calling story above.

OrthoFinder's clustering is protein-based, like RBH — it doesn't do the raw-genome-sequence verification this report's own correction required, so its species-specific counts still likely include some annotation-gap false positives of the dgat2_1 type. Treat it as corroboration of the order of magnitude, not a replacement for the verified 47/102 figures above.

03

Where the genomes actually differ

Functional-category profile (EggNOG/COG) of the corrected 102-gene, genuinely-confirmed #7-specific set, against the genome-wide baseline. An earlier version of this section, built on the un-corrected 472-gene set, reported a 5.6× transposon/recombination enrichment that does not hold up — see the correction notice above.

What survives, honestly

With the corrected, genuinely-confirmed #7-unique set at just 102 genes (88 of them still "hypothetical protein," 14 with any functional name, zero matching transposon/retroelement keywords), there is no clean functional-category story left to tell. The categories that show the largest fold-changes versus baseline (Defense mechanisms 9.5×, Nucleotide metabolism 5.8×) are each built from 1–2 genes out of the tiny 14-gene named subset — not a signal worth reporting as a finding, just noted here so the number doesn't quietly reappear uncaveated later. Lipid metabolism (category I) is not represented at all in the corrected unique set — the same conclusion as before (metabolism isn't where these strains diverge), just no longer resting on a transposon-enrichment story that turned out to be a measurement artifact.

The original, incorrect version of this section reported strain-specific genes as dominated by MIMI_R104 transposase, MIMI_R771 resolvase, and Gag-Pol/TNT-1-94 retroelement genes. All of those specific genes are present in HS6's raw genome sequence — they were simply never called as genes by BRAKER, most likely because repeat-masking ahead of ab initio gene prediction (standard practice, and probably deliberate in HS6's pipeline) excludes transposon-derived ORFs from the gene set entirely. Strain #7's MAKER pipeline, which builds gene models from combined evidence rather than pure ab initio prediction, called them anyway. This is an annotation-methodology difference between the two pipelines, not a biological difference in transposon content between the two strains. Retracted with the same visibility the original claim was made.

05

The Scaffolds_28 lead

The one locus where the cross-strain comparison surfaced something the single-strain analysis couldn't have found on its own.

1 — HS6's own PacBio coverage plot flagged an outlier
Genome-wide median long-read depth across HS6's 34 scaffolds is a tight 38–43× band — except Scaffolds_28 (1,129,389 bp), which sits at median 79×, 1.94× the genome baseline. Classic signature of a 2-copy region collapsed into one assembled sequence.
2 — strain #7 does not share the anomaly
#7's contig26 (1,030,349 bp) aligns to 96.7% of Scaffolds_28. Update: this was originally checked against #7's assembly-report baseline rather than #7's own raw reads; that gap has now been closed. #7's own raw HiFi reads were independently self-mapped to #7's own assembly (identical method to the HS6 side) and give 42.94× at contig26 vs. a 42–44× genome-wide baseline in #7 — a fully symmetric, apples-to-apples confirmation that carries completely normal single-copy depth. The duplication is specific to HS6's lineage, not a general feature of this genomic region across strains.
3 — what's actually in the region
239 genes sit on Scaffolds_28. Transferring functional annotation via the #7 orthology map identifies g10519 as mevalonate kinase (MVK) — an MVA-pathway enzyme in the same pathway as two other carotenoid-precursor genes already on HS6's candidate list (g12136, g3928, both confirmed conserved in Section 4).
4 — cross-checked against the original RNA-seq
In the original HS6 vs. wild-type #4 time-course, MVK trends down in HS6 at every timepoint (log2FC −0.71, −0.59, −0.10; overall log2FC −0.48, padj 0.33 — not significant at n=1, consistent direction across all three timepoints).
5 — systematic check across the whole pathway/regulator panel
Per-gene depth was recomputed directly (not just whole-scaffold averages) at all 24 pathway DEGs and MYB regulators from Sections 4 and 11.1, using both HS6's own HiFi self-alignment and the independent WT#4 short-read alignment. In the HS6 long-read data, only two genes sit above the ~40× baseline: g10519/MVK (78×) and g10428 (Myb-related protein A, 56×) — both on Scaffolds_28. Every other gene checked, including all 15 pathway genes from Section 4, sits at normal single-copy depth. The duplication is real, and it's confined to this one locus.
6 — an unresolved lead from the same scan
The WT#4 short-read alignment (genome-wide baseline ≈107×, confirmed by direct sampling) shows a second, unexpected pattern: genes on Scaffolds_22 and Scaffolds_30 read at ~185–217× — roughly 2× baseline, the same signature as Scaffolds_28. But HS6's own long-read self-alignment shows no elevation at these same loci (28–49×, normal range). Short reads are more prone to inflating apparent depth in repetitive regions that long reads resolve correctly, so this is more likely a short-read mapping artifact than a genuine WT-specific duplication — but it hasn't been independently confirmed or ruled out the way Scaffolds_28 has (no WT long-read data exists to check it the same way). Flagged, not claimed.
How to read this, honestly

A 2× dosage increase would naively predict higher expression, not lower — so this isn't a clean "extra copy → more enzyme → more flux" story. It's more consistent with a locus under active regulatory suppression despite elevated copy number, which is thematically coherent with HS6's selection history (EMS mutagenesis alongside a carotenoid-synthesis inhibitor, screened for higher lipid output — a strain actively pushed away from the MVA pathway's carotenoid branch). That's a hypothesis, not a conclusion.

Update: the duplication no longer rests solely on the vendor's plot. HS6's own raw PacBio HiFi reads (HS6.hifi_reads.fq.gz) were realigned independently to the HS6 assembly (minimap2, map-hifi preset) and per-scaffold depth recomputed directly: Scaffolds_28 = 79.45× against a genome-wide baseline tightly clustered at 38–43× everywhere else (98.65% of reads mapped) — matching the vendor figure almost exactly. The duplication is real and independently confirmed.

06

Validated candidate genes

Revised after the correction above. The original version of this section named three lipid-adjacent HS6-unique candidates; none survive.

Retraction

Methylsterol monooxygenase (g8002), phosphatidylglycerophosphate phosphatase (g6581), and acyl-CoA thioesterase (g5706) were originally reported here as HS6-specific, lipid-relevant candidates. Corrected genome-level verification (see Section 2) found all three sequences present in strain #7's raw genome at high identity — they were never called as genes by #7's MAKER pipeline, the same annotation-gap failure mode as dgat2_1. None of the three is a genuine HS6-vs-#7 difference.

The only gene that survives full verification — real SwissProt homology support and confirmed absence from #7's raw genome sequence — is g6782, a distant match (22.7% identity) to a viral major capsid protein from Chrysochromulina ericina virus. It has no clear lipid, carotenoid, or central-metabolism relevance. Given the low identity and viral origin, it plausibly reflects an integrated viral element rather than a host metabolic gene, and is not being proposed as a phenotype-relevant candidate.

Bottom line: no genuinely HS6-unique, metabolically-relevant gene survived verification against strain #7. This sharpens rather than weakens the report's central finding — the two strains really are close to identical at the gene-content level, and the Scaffolds_28/MVK lead in Section 5 remains the only substantive locus-level difference found anywhere in this comparison.

07

KEGG Mapper pathway comparison

KO assignment for both strains independently: HS6 via 5,180 genes mapped to 3,624 unique KOs through KEGG's REST API (existing SwissProt cross-references); strain #7 via its own full-proteome SwissProt search (5,831 hits) independently converted to 3,167 unique KOs through the same two-step KEGG API path — not transferred through the RBH orthology map. Each gene box below is split into two colored halves — left = HS6, right = strain #7 — teal where the KO is present, pale grey where absent.

How to read these maps

Earlier versions of this section transferred strain #7's KOs from HS6's via RBH, which meant a box could only ever show "HS6 only" or "both" — never "#7 only," by construction. That limitation is resolved: both strains now have independently-derived KO calls (3,938 total KOs; 2,853 shared, 771 HS6-only, 314 genuinely #7-only), so a "#7 only" box in the maps below is a real, independent result, not a structural blind spot. It still isn't the same rigor as the genome-level verification in Section 2 — a "#7 only" or "HS6 only" flag here means "no SwissProt-derived KO call on the other side," which can still reflect an annotation gap rather than a true absence. Treat individual boxes as leads, the same caution as everywhere else in this report.

08

Methods

Genome alignment

minimap2 (asm10 preset, --cs, 8 threads). Identity computed as alignment-length-weighted average of per-block de:f divergence tags. Coverage computed from merged, non-redundant aligned intervals per contig/scaffold.

Orthology

Bidirectional DIAMOND blastp (e-value <1e-5, max-target-seqs 5); reciprocal best hit by bitscore. Copy-number flags: any target gene serving as best hit for ≥3 distinct queries on the reciprocal side.

Genome-level verification

"Unique" protein candidates re-searched against the opposite strain's raw genome sequence via DIAMOND blastx (6-frame translation, sensitive mode, e-value <1e-5) — independent of either strain's gene annotation.

Functional categories

#7's EggNOG/COG categories (vendor-delivered, MAKER pipeline) transferred to HS6 genes via the RBH orthology map, avoiding a full local eggNOG-mapper database install.

Genome completeness & structure

compleasm (BUSCO-compatible, miniprot-based) against stramenopiles_odb12 — three separate BUSCO conda installs failed on dependency conflicts before this alternative worked. Telomere search via tidk (vendor-run, TTAGGG/CCCTAA repeat).

Promoter boundaries & orthogroups

StringTie (guided mode, -G reference GTF) on all 6 existing HISAT2 BAMs, merged, for evidence-based transcript boundaries in place of a flat upstream window. OrthoFinder 2.5.5 for formal orthogroup clustering as a cross-check on RBH (its downstream gene-tree step hit a numpy compatibility crash; the core orthogroup assignment completed before that and was used as-is).

All intermediate and output files retained under D:\HS6_vs_7_comparison\ (genomes / alignment / orthology / kegg / eggnog / results) — kept off the C: drive given its limited free space at time of analysis.

09

Limitations

  • Strain #7's DNA QC failed vendor spec on average fragment size, and its first RNA extraction failed QC (resequenced on a second sample that passed). Assembly and BUSCO metrics look solid regardless, but it's the same "don't hide the caveat" posture applied everywhere else in this project.
  • Reciprocal-best-hit was cross-checked against a full OrthoFinder run (Section 2) and the two agree closely (10,542 single-copy orthogroups vs. 11,463 RBH pairs) — RBH remains a simplified stand-in for complex gene-family history, but it isn't uncorroborated.
  • COG categories for HS6 exist only where an RBH ortholog was found in #7. HS6 genes without a #7 match have no category assigned at all — this is a coverage gap, not a "function unknown" call in the formal EggNOG sense.
  • The Scaffolds_28 duplication is now independently confirmed from HS6's own raw PacBio reads (Section 5) — this caveat, present in the original version of this report, is resolved.
  • A parameter bug in this report's own genome-level verification step went undetected until a spot-check caught it (see the correction notice at the top). The lesson generalizes: any "gene X is absent from genome Y" claim produced by a batch search tool needs a sanity-check on a known-real case before being trusted, regardless of how the search was set up.
  • The MVK expression trend is descriptive, not statistically significant — consistent with every other RNA-seq claim in this project, this rests on n=1 per genotype × timepoint (padj = 0.33).
  • No transcriptome exists for strain #7, so this comparison is genomic only. Any expression-level claim about #7 is not currently possible.
  • No epigenetic comparison was possible: strain #7 has native PacBio 5mC/CpG calls (2.7M sites); HS6's PacBio delivery did not include equivalent methylation data.
10

Recommended next steps

  • Test MVK copy number directly (ddPCR or a targeted long-read assembly check) now that the depth-based duplication signal is independently confirmed from raw reads.
  • Independent KO assignment for #7 is done (Section 7 now shows genuine "#7-only" pathway steps) — remaining open item is running the same rigor eggNOG-mapper would give for COG categories specifically, which Section 3's divergence analysis still lacks.
  • Sequence RNA-seq for strain #7 if it's to be used as a real comparator strain going forward — everything here is genomic; there is no expression-level cross-check yet.
  • Run a full OrthoFinder orthogroup analysis if this comparison is heading toward a manuscript — RBH is a fast, defensible first pass, but reviewers evaluating gene-family claims will expect formal orthogroup inference.
  • Treat the TE-enrichment finding as background, not signal, unless independent evidence suggests transposon activity is contributing to phenotypic instability in this lineage.
11

Follow-up: AI-intensive investigations

Four directions proposed after the strain comparison above. Two produced real findings, one was blocked by a public-service limitation (documented rather than papered over), and one isn't productive yet with only two genomes.

11.1 — Promoter motif discovery (real finding)

STREME (MEME Suite) was run de novo on the promoters (1 kb upstream) of all significantly up-regulated genes (n=398, padj<0.05, log2FC>0.5) and all significantly down-regulated genes (n=825) from the original HS6 vs. WT #4 time-course, each against a genome-wide background of all 16,087 gene promoters.

Top UP-set motif
CAAACCCGAAAC — P = 3.2×10⁻⁷ vs. background
Matching DOWN-set motif
CAAACCCCAAWC — P = 3.0×10⁻² vs. background (same core sequence)

The same motif core turned up independently as the top or near-top hit in both the up- and down-regulated gene sets — not something assumed going in. Scanning it back (FIMO) against the promoters of the specific pathway DEGs and MYB-family transcription factors from the trans-regulator screen finds it concentrated, with strong q-values, in exactly the down-regulated cluster:

GeneRoleBest matchq-value
g7955Long-chain FA-CoA ligase (pathway, ↓)CAAACCCGGAAC0.0018–0.018
g11711MYB3R-3 (regulator, ↓)CAGACCCGAAAT0.029–0.055
g3889Alkane monooxygenase (pathway, ↓)CAAAACCAGAAC0.029
g8263MYB3R-3 (2nd locus, regulator, ↓)CAAACAACAAAC0.065–0.18

What this does and doesn't show

This is co-occurrence, not binding proof — no ChIP-seq, no EMSA, no reporter assay. But it's a specific, falsifiable, mechanistically coherent picture: the motif sits in the promoters of the down-regulated MYB TFs and the down-regulated pathway genes they're the leading candidates to regulate, at moderate-to-strong statistical support (single-hypothesis, uncorrected for the multi-motif search — treat the individual q-values as suggestive, not confirmatory). The natural next step is exactly what Section 10 already recommends generally: an EMSA or yeast one-hybrid assay with a recombinant MYB DNA-binding domain against this specific motif.

Reconfirmed with better promoter boundaries: the flat 1 kb-upstream window used above is a crude stand-in for the true transcript start. Rerunning STREME on StringTie-assembled, evidence-based promoter boundaries (all 16,088 genes, Section 11.3's sibling analysis) reproduces the same motif core independently — CAAACCCSAAAC in the up-regulated set, CAAAMCCCAAAC in the down-regulated set (IUPAC ambiguity codes for the same G/C and A/C positions seen the first time). The motif isn't an artifact of the original window choice.

11.2 — Structure prediction for uncharacterized genes (blocked, documented)

Sequence-based search already came up empty for two genes: g14345 (298 aa, only MobiDBLite disorder calls from InterProScan, Section 22 of the wider project) and g6782 (the one gene that survived the corrected verification in Section 6, 22.7% identity to a viral capsid protein). Structure-level search — folding via ESMFold, then structural similarity search against PDB/AlphaFold-DB — can sometimes find distant homology invisible to sequence alignment.

The public ESMFold REST API (api.esmatlas.com) was reachable (a 3-residue test sequence returned HTTP 200 in under a second) but timed out on every real submission, including a shortened 150-aa fragment of g14345 — ruling out sequence length as the cause. This points to the free public endpoint being overloaded or rate-limited rather than anything fixable from this environment. Reported honestly as blocked, not worked around with a lower-quality substitute. A real attempt would need either local GPU infrastructure for ESMFold/ColabFold, or an authenticated API (e.g. NVIDIA BioNeMo, an AlphaFold server account) — outside what's available in this session.

11.3 — Metabolic network context for the MVA pathway

Rather than a full genome-scale metabolic model (which would need curated, organism-specific reconstruction and experimental exchange-flux data neither of which exist here — attempting one would produce a number that looks quantitative but isn't trustworthy), the DEG panel's KEGG KO assignments were used to pull the actual reaction chain they sit on:

MVA pathway: acetyl-CoA → isopentenyl diphosphate (IPP)
The universal precursor feeding sterol and carotenoid biosynthesis. Boxes show the four DEG-panel genes mapped onto their exact catalytic step.
Acetyl-CoA ×2→ g13563→ Acetoacetyl-CoA→ g3928→ HMG-CoA→ (HMGR, not in panel) → Mevalonate→ g10519 (MVK)→ Mevalonate-5-P→ (PMK, not in panel) → Mevalonate-5-PP→ g12136→ IPP

Three of the four panel genes on this chain (g13563, g3928, g12136) are the ones confirmed as clean 1:1 orthologs between HS6 and strain #7 in Section 4. g10519/MVK is the exception — sitting in the duplicated, down-trending Scaffolds_28 region — and it occupies the single reaction step immediately after the pathway's canonical rate-limiting enzyme (HMG-CoA reductase, not itself in this DEG panel). A real, connected 4-step substrate chain with one distinguishing node in the middle is a cleaner mechanistic picture than a gene list alone; it is still not proof of altered flux without a direct metabolite or isotope-tracing measurement.

g15357 (Pks13) has no KEGG KO at all — expected, not a lookup failure: thraustochytrid PUFA synthases are non-canonical PKS-type systems that standard KEGG orthology doesn't represent well (consistent with why the canonical Δ-desaturase steps of the ko01040 map in Section 7 are largely absent from this genome).

11.4 — Pangenome graph: not yet productive

A true pangenome graph (minigraph/pggb-style) earns its keep once there are enough genomes that presence/absence and structural variation can be called natively on the graph, without the pairwise annotation-mismatch problems this whole report has had to work around by hand (Sections 2 and the correction above). With exactly two genomes, a graph would encode the same information already captured by the Section 1 minimap2 alignment — no new finding to report, and building the infrastructure now would be demonstrating a tool, not doing research. Worth revisiting the moment a third Schizochytrium strain is sequenced.
